claim: Fewer than 10 bits per element are required for a 1% false positive probability, independent of the size of the set.
assumptions: The best whole number of hash functions is used for each size.
Measured on a set of 20,000 keys.
plan: Build real filters of 20,000 keys at sizes between 8 and 11 bits per key, probe 400,000 absent keys, and bisect for the smallest size that keeps false positives at or under 1%.
